newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience set to buy Darwin Molecular.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience set to buy Darwin Molecular.

text.p: Biotech specialist Chiroscience Group Plc said on Wednesday that it had agreed to buy Darwin Molecular Corporation for around $120 million.
Darwin is a privately owned gene-based biotechnology company, located in Seattle, Washington, US.

Chiroscience said it would issue between 17.4 and 21.3 million new ordinary shares to Darwin Shareholders depending on the market price of Chiroscience's shares over the ten days ending 16 December 1996.
Chiroscience said that the combination of Chiroscience and Darwin would provide access to further novel drug discovery programmes from genomics.

"By merging with Darwin, we have gained direct access to gene-based drug targets and genomics know-how that we believe will fuel our product pipeline in the coming years," said John Padfield, chief executive of Chiroscience.
Following completion of the agreement, two Darwin Directors will join the Board of Chiroscience.
In premarket trade, the shares jumped 21-1/2 pence to 370p after the news release.

Bill Gates, president and chief executive of Microsoft and a lead investor in Darwin, said, "There is a strong synergy between these two companies which should accelerate the translation of Darwin's excellent science into therapeutic products. This merger is the right move for both companies."
